whitePaper.title: The Unattended Hour
whitePaper.description: India registers ten million deaths a year and has no published standard for what happens in the hours after any of them. Twenty pages on why that gap exists, what it costs families, and why mobility is the spine of any standard worth writing.

article1.title: Why a family should never have to improvise a farewell
article1.excerpt: For too long, grieving families have had to make do with whatever transport they could find. We explore why that should never be — and how gentle, thoughtful care changes it.
article1.content:
In Indian society, ceremonial rites around life’s final transition carry immense spiritual and familial gravity. Yet, for generations, the mobility infrastructure connecting hospitals, homes, and ceremonial grounds remained virtually unexamined.

The Problem of Improvised Vehicles

Commercial utility vans retrofitted with basic metal biers often lacked sound dampening, proper climate control, or reverent interior lighting. Emergency medical ambulances, pressed into service as mortuary vans, brought hospital sirens and clinical harshness to a moment that called for peaceful composure.

Purpose-Built, With Care

Eternal was created to replace improvised, impersonal arrangements with something gentler and more dignified. By insulating cabin acoustics, introducing gentle, dignified handling, and integrating soft warm cove lighting, ceremonial mobility becomes a serene sanctuary for grieving families.

article2.title: How hospitals can care for families, right to the end
article2.excerpt: A family’s care doesn’t end at discharge. A gentle look at how hospitals can make sure grieving families are held, right to the end.
article2.content:
More and more hospitals are recognising that care doesn’t end at discharge. How a family is treated in their moment of loss says everything about an institution’s heart.

What thoughtful care looks like

1. Cared for: immaculate, gently sanitised interiors, tended between every journey.
2. Dependable: a reliable presence you can count on, whenever a family needs it.
3. Gentle people: calm, softly-spoken team members, trained in grief sensitivity and discretion.
